stories.title: Washington Judge Keeps Zillow Antitrust Suit Alive Over Mortgage Steering Claims
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that a federal judge in Washington has denied Zillow's request to reconsider an earlier ruling, so the proposed antitrust class action Dupuis v. Zillow can continue on its mortgage steering claims. The suit alleges Zillow pressured affiliated agents to steer buyers to its mortgage products. The ruling does not decide the merits.
stories.hook: Zillow loses bid to reconsider, keeping mortgage steering antitrust claims alive in Washington

stories.title: AI Connectors For E-Discovery: Great To Drive, But There Are Speed Limits
stories.hook: Onna's Claude collection tool shows AI chat logs are now discoverable, and training matters

stories.title: Harvey Forum Chicago: GCs Talk About Increasing Expectations Due to AI
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports on a Harvey Forum in Chicago where general counsel discussed rising expectations of AI. Robert Rivkin, chief legal officer at United Airlines, said companies will likely try to do as much as possible with AI before assigning matters to outside counsel. The extract is a single quote, so the wider discussion is not visible.
stories.hook: United Airlines CLO expects clients to exhaust AI before sending work to outside counsel

stories.title: NCSC scheme will help critical organisations test their cyber defences
stories.ltme_summary: The National Cyber Security Centre has launched its Cyber Adversary Simulation (CyAS) scheme, an assurance scheme for suppliers of adversary simulation testing. The NCSC says providers will be assessed against an NCSC-defined standard and will build customer-specific attack plans. The scheme starts as a minimum viable product, letting the NCSC test demand before a fuller operating model. It sits alongside the Cyber Assessment Framework and the Cyber Resilience Audit scheme.
stories.hook: NCSC launches CyAS scheme to assure providers of realistic adversary simulation testing for critical organisations

stories.title: Morning Docket: 11.11.26
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's Morning Docket for 11 November 2026 rounds up US legal news. Items include an ethics charge against Alina Habba over an NDA dispute, a judge removing a DOJ attorney from a case, and a Texas incoming chief justice proposing to restore an ABA accreditation requirement. The newsletter also covers SEC enforcement figures and a defamation suit against the BBC.
stories.hook: Morning Docket flags Texas plans to bring back ABA accreditation requirement after the midterms

stories.title: Legora Targets Public Sector With Ex-Minister
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer reports that Legora is expanding Lucy Frazer KC's role, from adviser since July to leading its public sector work, and says she will be part-time and based in London. Legora says courts and government legal teams need AI they can trust. The company cites the Crown Court backlog of 80,829 cases at the end of June 2026.
stories.hook: Legora makes Lucy Frazer KC its public sector lead, pitching AI to governments and courts

stories.title: Mercedes Lawyer Joins AI Native Compound Law
stories.hook: Compound Law hires ex-Mercedes-Benz counsel as it builds an AI-native, fixed-fee firm in Berlin

stories.title: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger
‘We now ask the AI first’ – exclusive new research reveals how AI is transforming in-house legal
stories.hook: 82 per cent of in-house teams already implement generative AI, according to a Legal Business and Thomson Reuters survey

stories.title: Nvidia brings in Wachtell for investigation into CEO’s alleged affair with Chinese spy
Sullivan & Cromwell rescues current and future trainees as Weil partners approve wind-down
Keystone’s AI funds tool – “We’re solving a problem using tech in the right way”
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider has published an interview headlined around Keystone's AI funds tool, in which the company says it is solving a problem using technology in the right way. The extract available here is only a site verification notice, so the substance of the interview cannot be confirmed from it.
stories.hook: Keystone's AI funds tool is pitched as a practical use of technology, according to an interview

stories.title: Former Cabinet minister Lucy Frazer KC to lead public sector drive by Legora
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that Lucy Frazer KC is to lead Legora's public sector work, according to the headline. The extract available is a site verification notice, so the detail of her role cannot be checked from it. Artificial Lawyer separately reports that Frazer, a former Cabinet minister, will lead public sector partnerships.
stories.hook: Lucy Frazer KC to lead Legora's public sector push, a move the legal AI vendor is pitching to governments

stories.title: GenieAI “spins up entire team of agents for each workflow”
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider has published a piece on GenieAI, quoting the company's claim that it spins up an entire team of agents for each workflow. The extract available is a site verification notice, so the detail of the product cannot be confirmed from it. GenieAI has published a large run of product pages in the same period.
stories.hook: GenieAI says it spins up a whole team of agents for each legal workflow

stories.title: How Lisa’s Law migrated 14 years of data to LEAP Enterprise
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Practice Management reports that Lisa's Law, a London firm of around 75 people, moved from a case management system it had used since 2012 to LEAP Enterprise. The firm migrated 73 users and 14 years of matter data, with Thinkwild also involved. The article is presented as a vendor-supported case study from LEAP.
stories.hook: Lisa's Law moved 73 users and 14 years of matter data to LEAP Enterprise

stories.title: Latham puts $1m behind its associates’ best AI ideas
Willkie adds Hogan Lovells Cadwalader PE head in five-partner transatlantic raid
Weil partners vote to formally wind down Wall Street firm
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Weil Gotshal and Manges partners voted 97 per cent in favour of an orderly wind-down, handing the process to a committee. About 1,200 lawyers and more than 1,000 staff are affected. The Gazette says Sidley Austin is in talks to hire around 200 from Weil and that Kirkland & Ellis will take 40 Weil lawyers.
stories.hook: Weil partners vote 97 per cent to wind down the firm, with Sidley and Kirkland among those hiring

stories.title: Lords clash over 'Stalin' clause in courts bill
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that peers clashed over a clause in the Courts and Tribunals Bill that would let ministers add offences to the non-jury list without full parliamentary scrutiny. Lord Keen of Elie criticised the 'Henry VIII powers' and withdrew his amendment, with the issue to return at report stage. Lord Lemos said the power would let the system respond to evolving fraud, including developments in AI.
stories.hook: Peers challenge ministerial power to add offences to the non-jury list in the Courts and Tribunals Bill

stories.title: Industry panel event highlights property law’s biggest threat: AI competition, part one
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer carries a summary of a Search Acumen panel at the Digital Conveyancing Summit in October. The panel addressed AI competition as a threat to property law, according to the outlet, and this is part one of a series. The extract is only an outline, so the panel's conclusions are not visible here.
stories.hook: Search Acumen panel frames AI competition as property law's biggest threat

stories.title: Claren launches Envoys to take on in-house legal work
stories.ltme_summary: Claren has launched Envoys, which it describes as AI employees for in-house legal teams. According to the outline, Envoys picks up requests from Slack, Teams and email and escalates risky items. The extract is a single summary line, so further product detail is not available here.
stories.hook: Claren launches Envoys, AI employees that take in-house legal requests from Slack, Teams and email

stories.title: HIGHCOURT launches offline agentic AI system for law firms
stories.hook: HIGHCOURT launches an agentic legal operating system that runs on firms' own machines

stories.title: Piepenbrock v LSE: EAT rules on bankruptcy and standing to pursue employment appeals
ABA President Barbara Howard says association will continue to prioritize the defense of democracy
Weil Gotshal partners vote to dissolve firm
stories.ltme_summary: Weil, Gotshal & Manges partners have voted to dissolve the nearly century-old firm, with 97 per cent approving according to Law.com. A three-person committee will oversee the wind-down, with restructuring officers from AlixPartners and Davis Polk. Law.com also reports that the restructuring chair Matt Barr and several bankruptcy lawyers are in talks to join Skadden, and that the firm lost nearly 50 partners in 2026.
stories.hook: Weil Gotshal partners vote 97 per cent to dissolve the firm

stories.title: What happened at Weil Gotshal? Could tech help other firms avoid that fate?
stories.ltme_summary: ABA Journal's Legal Rebels podcast interviews Noah Waisberg, CEO of Zuva and a former Weil Gotshal associate, about the firm's wind-down and whether technology could help other firms avoid a similar fate. Waisberg previously led Kira Systems, which was sold to Litera in 2021. The episode is by Victor Li.
stories.hook: Zuva CEO Noah Waisberg asks whether technology could have helped Weil Gotshal avoid its wind-down

stories.title: The ACLU Doesn’t Do Impeachment, But It Had Some Thoughts About Pete Hegseth
Is Cahill Gordon The Next Weil? Partner Exits And Acquisition Talk Have Biglaw Guessing
Chuck Grassley Says Democrats Are Stonewalling Judges ‘For The First Time In Our Nation’s History.’ Merrick Garland Would Like A Word.
Claren Launches ‘Envoys’ Inhouse Agents
stories.hook: Claren launches Envoys, always-on agents for in-house legal teams

stories.title: Legora Taps Ex-Solicitor General To Boost Public Sector Deals
stories.ltme_summary: Law360 Pulse reports that Legora has hired a former Solicitor General to build its public sector business. The extract is only the outlet summary line, so the individual's name, start date and remit are not available here. The item is a people move at an AI legal technology vendor.
stories.hook: Legora hires an ex-Solicitor General to grow its public sector deals

stories.title: ‘It can get really ugly’ – Weil braces for litigation as wind-down begins
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Weil, Gotshal & Manges is braced for litigation as its wind-down begins. Albert Togut of Togut Segal & Segal is quoted saying that all those involved in law firm failure are lawyers, so any of them can start litigation without outside counsel. The extract also lists related Weil coverage, including a partner vote on the wind-down plan.
stories.hook: Weil braces for litigation as its wind-down begins, with a bankruptcy adviser warning claims may come from inside the profession

stories.title: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger talks
Latham unveils $1 million bonus pot to reward lawyers driving AI innovation
stories.ltme_summary: Latham & Watkins has launched a $1 million awards programme, the Associate AI Impact Award, to reward associates who build AI tools or improve workflows. The firm has set aside the sum for 2027 and says all associates across its global offices may take part. Michael Rubin, chair of the firm's AI practice, says the award aims to scale useful ideas. Winners have not yet been named.
stories.hook: Latham & Watkins puts $1 million behind an associate award for AI tool building and workflow ideas

stories.title: New judicial review guidance explained – AI use & urgent applications
stories.ltme_summary: Brabners, writing for Legal Futures, explains new Administrative Court guidance. The Judicial Review Guide 2026 adds a section on AI tools, warning court users to take reasonable care when citing authorities, and sets page limits. A separate Practice Statement tightens urgent applications, with urgency judged solely on Form N463. Brabners says the guidance is essential reading for parties to judicial review.
stories.hook: Administrative Court's 2026 Judicial Review Guide adds an AI section and says urgency will be judged on Form N463 alone

stories.title: BigHand Report finds law firms restructuring for AI without managing the cost of delivery
stories.ltme_summary: BigHand's Law Firm Talent and Resourcing Report 2026, based on a survey of more than 800 law firm leaders in the UK and North America, finds that AI is changing hiring for nearly all firms but few track matter profitability. Clients are pressing on AI-related pricing, according to 46 per cent of firms. BigHand says 16 per cent combine structured processes, technology and budgets. DLA Piper is cited as a customer.
stories.hook: BigHand report: 99% of law firms say AI is changing hiring, but only 22% weigh matter profitability

stories.title: Practice-area searches to law firms fell 36% this summer as name searches held steady, research finds
stories.ltme_summary: MLT Digital's report Search Has Moved. Has Your Firm? uses Google data from 99 law firm websites in Scotland, England and Wales, and Ireland. It finds that clicks for practice-area searches fell 35.8 per cent between June and August 2026, against the same months of 2025, while firm-name searches held steady. MLT links the drop partly to Google AI Overviews, and the agency is offering a free review.
stories.hook: MLT Digital says practice-area clicks to law firm sites fell 35.8% this summer, while name searches held steady

stories.title: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off merger talks
Hogan Lovells Cadwalader adds HSF Kramer DCM head in London
Stephenson Harwood - Taylor Wessing merger called off
stories.ltme_summary: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing say they will not proceed with a planned merger, which had been under discussion and was due for a partner vote by the end of 2026 ahead of a possible May 2027 combination. The joint statement cites initial discussions and mutual agreement. Taylor Wessing became independent in June after its UK arm merged with Winston & Strawn.
stories.hook: Stephenson Harwood and Taylor Wessing call off planned merger

stories.title: Solicitor appeals strike-off over Munich remote-hearing lie
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Priyank Tanwar, struck off in January 2026, is appealing the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal's finding that he misled Leicester County Court about his location during an August 2023 hearing. His counsel argues the tribunal over-relied on the transcript. The SRA opposed the appeal, which was heard before Thomas Raphael KC, sitting as a deputy High Court judge.
stories.hook: Struck-off solicitor Priyank Tanwar argues the SDT over-relied on a transcript in his Munich remote-hearing appeal

stories.title: Form: Apply for a court order to make arrangements for a child or resolve a dispute about their upbringing: Form C100
stories.ltme_summary: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated Form C100, the application for a child arrangements, prohibited steps or specific issue order under the Children Act 1989. The form can be filed online or on paper, and a mediation information meeting is required before most applications. The page history records an 11 November 2026 update to the Welsh form.
stories.hook: HMCTS updates Form C100 child arrangements application, with the Welsh version revised on 11 November 2026

stories.title: Form: Apply for an inherent jurisdiction order in relation to children: Form C66
stories.hook: HMCTS adds a Welsh page and updated Welsh form for C66, the inherent jurisdiction application for children

stories.title: Form: Apply to internationally transfer a court application involving children to or from England and Wales: Form C68
stories.hook: HMCTS adds a Welsh page and form for C68, the international transfer of children's cases

stories.title: Guidance: Gender Recognition Certificate: list of medical practitioners in gender dysphoria
stories.hook: HMCTS updates its Gender Recognition Certificate list of medical practitioners, revising the London Gender Identity Clinic entry

stories.title: Guidance: Expert adviser on the future of criminal courts for children
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice appoints David Ormerod KC as expert adviser on criminal courts for children, reporting by August 2027

stories.title: Why Blue California Voters Rejected Implementing The Nation’s First Wealth Tax
No Just Moving On: We Demand Vengeance Against MAGA, And Getting It Will Help Lower Costs
Congressional Democrats Are Ready To Turn Up The Heat On Biglaw’s Trump Deals
D&L: Daeryook & Aju and Lin Merge in South Korea
stories.ltme_summary: Daeryook & Aju and Lin signed a merger agreement in Seoul on 9 November 2026 to form D&L. The combined firm will have 397 Korean-licensed lawyers and combined 2025 revenue of 143.7 billion won, and the firms expect registration in mid-December 2026 or later. Daeryook & Aju will be the surviving entity, and the firms describe the deal as a merger of equals.
stories.hook: Daeryook & Aju and Lin sign merger agreement to form D&L in South Korea

stories.title: Vote for the top insurance defence specialized firms 2027-28
BigLaw Breakaways Fuel Kindleworth’s New York Expansion as Partners Seek Independence
Does Your Budget Tell You No, or Tell You Where to Go?
Court wants to know if Keker law firm is still representing Perplexity AI
stories.source_name: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

seen_in.source_name: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.ltme_summary: Commentator Edward Lee reports that Judge Engelmayer has asked whether Keker Van Nest still represents Perplexity AI or intends to withdraw. The question follows Perplexity's late withdrawal of its motion to have Proskauer act for it, after Proskauer raised a potential conflict from its earlier work for the opposing party. The post sits within a tracker of AI copyright and tort litigation.
stories.hook: Judge Engelmayer asks whether Keker still represents Perplexity AI

stories.title: Less is More: SEC’s Division of Enforcement Year-End Results Reflect Shift Toward More Targeted Enforcement Amid Decline in Actions and Monetary Remedies
stories.ltme_summary: The Debevoise & Plimpton client note reports that the SEC's Division of Enforcement announced fiscal 2026 results on 10 November 2026, the first full year under Chairman Paul Atkins and the first annual results under Director David Woodcock. The headline points to a shift to more targeted enforcement and fewer actions. The extract is only a summary line.
stories.hook: Debevoise reads SEC fiscal 2026 enforcement results as a shift to fewer, more targeted cases

stories.title: OCC’s New “Super Intelligence” Supervisory Framework: Key Takeaways and How It Compares to the FSB’s AI Sound Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Debevoise & Plimpton reviews the OCC's Supervisory Framework for Bank Use of Super Intelligence and compares it with the FSB's AI sound practices. The firm says the framework signals how US bank regulators may approach AI supervision.
entities: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency

stories.title: Digital Fairness Act: the EU’s new consumer protection rulebook takes shape | Freshfields
stories.ltme_summary: Freshfields analyses the European Commission's Digital Fairness Act proposal, published on 11 November 2026. The proposal would replace the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive with a directly applicable Regulation covering dark patterns, influencer marketing, subscriptions and addictive design. It would also let the Commission investigate directly and impose fines.
stories.hook: Freshfields says the Digital Fairness Act would replace the UCPD with an EU Regulation

stories.title: Ninth Circuit Leaves Core California Emissions Disclosures in Place | Morrison Foerster
stories.ltme_summary: The Ninth Circuit declined to block SB 253's Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions disclosures but held Scope 3 and SB 261 likely breach the First Amendment, according to Morrison Foerster. The opinion is not a final merits ruling.

stories.title: CFTC Declares DCMs’ Use of Geographic Access Restrictions Inconsistent With Impartial Access Requirements | Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP
stories.ltme_summary: Skadden says the CFTC has approved guidance on 5 November 2026 that designated contract markets generally may not restrict access based on a trader's location within the US. DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions within 30 days or explain why they cannot comply. The guidance responds to state court orders against prediction markets offering sports event contracts.
stories.hook: CFTC bars geographic access limits at US futures exchanges within 30 days

stories.title: Oman data privacy tool
stories.ltme_summary: Trowers & Hamlins has published a free online Data Privacy maturity assessment tool for businesses preparing for Oman's PDPL. Users receive a maturity assessment, commentary and recommended next steps across awareness, governance, consent, data subject rights and security. The extract is a short product notice and gives no publication date.
stories.hook: Trowers & Hamlins offers a free PDPL maturity assessment for Oman

stories.title: CFTC Addresses Domestic Geographic Restrictions on DCM Access
stories.ltme_summary: Willkie Farr & Gallagher has published a note on a CFTC position addressing domestic geographic restrictions on designated contract market access. The extract is only an outlet summary line, so the detail of the CFTC position is not visible here. The note concerns derivatives market access rather than legal technology.
stories.hook: Willkie outlines CFTC position on domestic geographic limits for DCM access

stories.title: Ninth Circuit Finds Certain Aspects of California’s Climate Risk Disclosure Laws Likely Unconstitutional, While Preserving Core Emissions Reporting Requirements
stories.ltme_summary: Willkie Farr & Gallagher reports that the Ninth Circuit found some aspects of California's climate risk disclosure laws likely unconstitutional, while keeping core emissions reporting requirements in place.

stories.title: Bevan Brittan expands with new partner
Ministry of Justice cuts impact court support
stories.ltme_summary: Support Through Court, a national charity helping people in civil and family courts, says a £300,000 funding cut from the Ministry of Justice has closed its services in Chelmsford and Southend. The charity says it assisted on 51,116 occasions last year and is appealing for the decision to be reversed. Its chief executive Emma Taylor and former Supreme Court President Lord Neuberger both voiced concern.
stories.hook: A £300,000 Ministry of Justice cut has closed court support services in Chelmsford and Southend

stories.title: Kindleworth expands operations with New York office
stories.ltme_summary: Kindleworth, a London-based consultancy that helps lawyers launch their own firms, has opened a New York office. Maryana Kodner joins as Partner and Head of US Operations, and Anand David as Strategic Advisor. The firm says it has supported over 50 law firm launches globally.
stories.hook: Kindleworth opens New York office to help US partners launch their own firms

stories.title: Protect the Value You Negotiate with Ironclad + Ramp | Ironclad
stories.ltme_summary: Ironclad promotes a December webinar with Ramp on linking procurement, legal and finance in one contract workflow. The vendor says about 11 per cent of contract value leaks after signature. The session will demonstrate purchase requests triggering Ironclad contract workflows and synced obligations.
stories.hook: Ironclad and Ramp say about 11 per cent of contract value leaks after signature

stories.title: What Is a Gap Assessment? A Guide for Legal Teams
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic publishes a guide explaining gap assessments for legal departments and law firms. It distinguishes gap assessment from risk assessment and describes compliance gaps as unmet, partly met or undocumented requirements. The article argues that governed AI use is the most urgent current gap and that visibility of AI tools is usually the first step.
stories.hook: Neota Logic says ungoverned AI tools are the most common gap in legal teams

stories.title: AI Accuracy, Capability, and Reliability: What's the Difference? | Relativity Blog | Relativity
stories.ltme_summary: Relativity says legal teams should separate the terms accurate, capable and reliable when evaluating AI tools. Accuracy concerns a single correct output, capability means a tool can do a task, and reliability means consistent performance at scale. Aurora Bryant, senior manager of applied legal intelligence at Relativity, is quoted on the distinctions.
stories.hook: Relativity separates accurate, capable and reliable AI for legal teams

stories.title: How AI Thought It Earned Its Rigor Badge (and Failed the Test)
SEC’s FY 2026 Enforcement Results Show Fewer Cases, Sharper Priority Signals
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reviews the SEC's fiscal 2026 enforcement results, announced on 10 November, which show fewer actions but a focus on investor protection, public-company reporting and trading integrity. The article notes an action involving Archer-Daniels-Midland and suggests in-house counsel should not relax controls.
stories.hook: SEC fiscal 2026 enforcement results show fewer cases and sharper priorities

stories.title: How Should Legal Teams Evaluate Legal Hold Software?: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Shelley Bougnague of Cloudficient argues that legal hold software should be judged as a preservation system, not just a tool for notices and acknowledgments. She recommends testing products against realistic matter scenarios. The post promotes Cloudficient's CaseFusion product, which covers identification, legal hold and targeted collection, and is published on eDiscovery Today with a disclosure that Cloudficient is a sponsor.
stories.hook: Cloudficient urges legal teams to test legal hold tools as preservation systems

stories.title: Getting the Workflow Right and Preparing for What’s Coming with AI: Artificial Intelligence Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Discernis, a sponsor of eDiscovery Today, argues that in-house counsel should treat AI as an investigative intelligence tool rather than an automation tool in corporate investigations. The final part of its series covers workflow structure, regulatory context and preparation. The post stresses that AI handles high-volume review well but cannot exercise legal judgment.
stories.hook: Discernis says in-house counsel should treat AI as an investigative tool, not automation

stories.title: MPs call for legislation to overturn Carter-Ruck privilege ruling
stories.ltme_summary: MPs are urging the government to legislate so that the September High Court ruling in Carter-Ruck does not stop regulators reaching privileged material. Labour MP Phil Brickell, speaking on the second reading of the Financial Services and Markets Bill, warned of a risk that wrongdoing by solicitors would go unscrutinised. The bill would move AML supervision of lawyers and accountants to the FCA, with the transition due to begin in 2028.
stories.hook: MPs want the FCA to access privileged material after the Carter-Ruck ruling

stories.title: Former judge sets out how to do “the best job in the world”
stories.ltme_summary: Sir Peter Coulson, retiring from the Court of Appeal, has published a book, The Practice of Judging, and spoke to Legal Futures about judicial life. He discusses rising workloads, the three-month judgment expectation and the growing number of litigants in person. He says he is sympathetic to their use of AI, describing it as often the only friend they have.
stories.hook: Sir Peter Coulson says litigants in person turning to AI are often without other support

stories.title: Law firms taking out more and bigger loans to fund growth
stories.ltme_summary: Barclays research of 125 senior leaders finds that 93 per cent of law firms are likely to increase investment over the next year. Loan balances among legal practices rose 12.7 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 on the year, and 32 per cent of firms say they have redesigned their business model to use AI fully. Skilled labour shortages affect 63 per cent of firms' growth.
stories.hook: Barclays data shows law firm loan balances up 12.7 per cent as firms fund AI and growth

stories.title: From chat to Cowork: preparing your law firm for agentic AI
stories.ltme_summary: Matthew Stringer, founder and CEO of Legal Futures, writes that law firms should weigh agentic AI before moving further into it. He separates conversational AI from agents that plan steps and act across connected systems, and describes standing mandates that let an agent act on defined events. He proposes five tests for any use: repeatable, checkable, supervised, bounded and worth it. Stridon, his consultancy, estimates an agent briefing could cost around £2-5.
stories.hook: Stringer sets out five tests for law firms before delegating work to agentic AI

stories.title: Property sales expectations drop to weakest level since July 2023
Solicitor fined £10,500 over AML and account breaches
stories.hook: SDT fines a sole manager £10,500 for accounts rules and AML breaches

stories.title: Half of homebuyers would pull out of purchase if the home had a flood risk
Government invests £2.4m to give small businesses discount on cyber protections
Trustees being forced out of mainstream banking, STEP warns
Solicitor fined £10,500 over AML and account breaches
stories.ltme_summary: This page carries the same headline as the SDT fine story, but its extract is an unrelated item about trustees being forced out of mainstream banking, according to STEP. The extract does not confirm the fine itself, so the underlying story should be checked against the original report.
stories.hook: SDT fines a sole manager £10,500 for accounts rules and AML breaches

stories.title: Compliance with Celeste: Trust, not just technology
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp describes Celeste, its Firm AI product, as an operating layer for professional firms, and explains how firms can keep control. Celeste uses the requesting user's credentials, admins choose the model for each job, and a person reviews requests before submission. The post sets out chat, assistant and coworker layers and promotes the product.
stories.hook: Intapp says Celeste works within firms' existing permissions and model choices

stories.title: The Third Partner: Why Shepherd & Co. Trusts Dye & Durham for Cashiering
stories.ltme_summary: Dye & Durham, in a vendor feature in Quill, describes how Shepherd & Co. outsources cashiering to a dedicated Dye & Durham cashier. The piece says reconciliations were brought up to date within about a fortnight after the partners took over, and that the arrangement has run for seven years.
stories.hook: Shepherd & Co. credits Dye & Durham outsourced cashiering with clean monthly reconciliations
